ideas.angle: Brake fluid absorbs moisture from the air over time. On a long ghat descent it can boil, and the pedal then sinks to the floor. This is why makers say to change it about every 2-3 years.
ideas.hook_line_en: Your brake fluid can boil, and then the pedal goes straight to the floor.
ideas.why: Almost nobody knows brake fluid has an expiry date. Anyone who drives the Tirumala or Araku ghats feels the risk is real.

ideas.angle: Going from 50 to 100 km/h doubles the speed but needs about four times the braking distance. The brain feels it as only twice.
ideas.hook_line_en: At 100 km/h your car needs 4 times the braking distance, not 2.
ideas.why: Everyone drives fast on the Hyderabad ORR and the Vijayawada highway. A shocking number that changes how they see speed will stop them.

ideas.angle: A tyre with deep tread can still be dangerous once it is 5-6 years old, because the rubber hardens and loses grip. The 4-digit date code on the sidewall tells you its age.
ideas.hook_line_en: Your tyre has a secret date stamped on it, and it may already be expired.
ideas.why: They can go and check their own car in 10 seconds. It is a hidden fact on something they own, so it is easy to share in the family group.

ideas.topic: ESC: the computer that stops your skid
ideas.angle: Electronic stability control brakes single wheels on its own when it senses a slide. That is why a car can swerve around a barrier instead of sliding straight into it. Our two scenes show the without and with side by side.
ideas.hook_line_en: Your car has a computer that brakes one wheel by itself to save you from a skid.
ideas.why: It is a curiosity-gap hook with the result shown first. The brake_skid versus brake_swerve contrast is our strongest visual, and it makes people ask whether their own car has it.

ideas.angle: On a wet NH, a worn tyre can ride on a film of water above roughly 80 km/h. Then the steering and brakes do nothing for a moment. This is the same reason a scooter slides on a wet road.
ideas.hook_line_en: In monsoon, your car can float on water and you lose steering completely.
ideas.why: Monsoon driving on NH-65 and the Vizag roads is a real fear. Seeing the car lose control with the wheels still turning is a visual shock.

idea.angle: Old advice to pump the brake makes an ABS car worse. ABS already pumps about 15 times a second, so you should press hard and hold. Verify the exact pulse rate against a manufacturer source before scripting.
idea.hook_line_en: Who told you to pump the brake? In an ABS car, that's wrong.
idea.why: Almost every Telugu driver was taught to pump the brakes by an uncle or a driving school, and this tells them that habit can hurt them.

facts.claim: Manufacturer pulse rates differ. Bosch says its ABS can reduce and rebuild brake pressure up to 40 times a second when a wheel is about to lock. A BMW ABS training document gives 2 to 15 pulses per second. HowStuffWorks says some systems cycle up to 15 times a second. So '15 a second' is a typical upper figure, not an exact universal one. The script says 'up to 15, some systems even more', not 'exactly 15'. I could not open the Bosch page directly, so the 40 figure comes from the search snippet. Re-check it before publishing.
BMW technical training document on ABS fundamentals: the pulsing rate is 2-15 times per second.
Some ABS systems can cycle up to 15 times per second.
Honda owner's manual: never pump the brake pedal. The pedal may pulsate slightly when ABS is working.
Nissan Juke 2024 owner's manual: apply firm, steady pressure and do not pump the brakes. Pumping may increase stopping distance.
Mazda CX-3 owner's manual: slight pedal vibration and chattering noise are normal. Keep the pedal pressed without pumping.
Lexus RX300 manual: hold the brake pedal down firmly and do not pump it.
Mechanism: wheel speed sensors feed the ECU. When a wheel is about to lock, the hydraulic unit's valves hold, release and reapply pressure faster than a driver can.

plan.promise: You'll know why you should never pump the brake in an ABS car: the car already pumps it up to 15 times a second. Press hard, hold, and steer.
plan.aha: Pumping with your foot fights ABS. The car already does it much faster, so your job is to press hard, hold, and steer.
plan.takeaway: In an emergency in an ABS car, press the brake pedal hard and hold it. Feel the pulsing, don't lift off, and steer around the obstacle.

predicted_retention_risks: Beats 8-10 (sensor, ECU, valves) are a technical chain. The twist at beat 11 has to arrive fast, and the X-ray visuals have to change every beat.
The fact_card beats (11-12) are number-heavy. The line 'Mee kaalu antha fast ga pump cheyyaledu' is a soft claim, so it is less punchy than a hard figure.
